input: grid is a rectangular R by C binary integer array, with 1 for land and 0 for water. Empty outer arrays and zero-column rows are supported. Total R * C is within the shared collection-size bound. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. JavaScript integers are primitive safe-integer Number values, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Nonnegative integer number of land cells with no cardinal land-only path to any boundary cell. Empty grids return zero.
mutation_aliasing: Input grid, all rows and all values are unchanged; shared row identities are acceptable because the grid is read-only. Visited rows and queue records are private. The Solution object retains no state.
numeric: Coordinate and result arithmetic is bounded by R * C; every boundary cell is seeded once by the nested index loop, including one-row/one-column grids. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(R * C + R + 1) time and O(R * C + R + 1) auxiliary space. Every land cell is enqueued at most once, marked on enqueue. Queue uses a head cursor; processed entries remain allocated and are included in the space bound. Bounds use bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time array indexing and amortized append/pop; output and built-in allocation costs are included.

helpers.name: cardinalNeighbors
helpers.contract: Yields exactly the in-bounds cardinal neighbors in up/right/down/left order, never the current cell or diagonal cells. All coordinate pairs are local.
